messages.author: 85679393b8bc3d9b
messages.subject: slider file and gpagen
parts:
Hi all,

I have semi-landmarks that I want to use with gpagen but I'm not sure if they need to be in order. Landmark positions 1:4 are fixed, 5:29 are semi, 30:54 are semi, and 55:79 are semi. Just curious if geomorph will interepret the slider file (attached) the way I have it or should I be formatting it some other way. Thank you.

Nick

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] slider file and gpagen
parts:
Looks fine, Nick, although without knowing your digitizing scheme it is tricky to say. Anyway, the sliders definition lines do not need to be in any particular order, what does matter is to get the before-slider-after sequence right.

At any rate, this will be easy to also verify after gpa. Once you have performed superimposition, use plot(my.gpa) or plotAllSpecimens(my.gpa$coords) to check the superimposed data. While the landmarks will (generally, depending on your sample) have spherical distributions of the points around those of the average shape, the semilandmarks will not, particularly if you slide using Procrustes distance.

Hope this helps

Antigoni

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] slider file and gpagen
parts:
Nick, your superimposed data look OK, although you are the best person to judge that, being more familiar with the system and digitizing scheme.

You can use bilat.symmetry to obtain the symmetric shapes, but beware that in that case you are eliminating biological asymmetries in addition to any user-introduced effects. Just a matter of definition, nothing wrong with doing that, to my view, if you are not interested in asymmetry as a biological pattern.

Hope this helps!

Antigoni
